How to Remove Your Home Address, Phone Number and Email from Google

By RMA — Web Reputation Agency

Google will remove search results that expose your home address, personal phone number or private email, and in most cases you can request it yourself through the "Results about you" tool in a few minutes. Removal from Google does not delete the page, so the lasting fix combines a Google request with a GDPR erasure request to the website that published the data.

What Google's personal information policy covers

Google accepts removal requests for results that display personally identifiable contact details or data that could lead to fraud or harassment. The policy applies worldwide, so a resident of Turin or Naples can use it without proving any particular harm.

The categories Google lists include:

  • physical home addresses and private contact information such as phone numbers and personal email addresses;
  • government identification numbers, including tax codes and passport or identity card numbers;
  • bank account and payment card numbers, signatures and login credentials;
  • images of handwritten signatures or ID documents and confidential medical records;
  • content published with the intent to harass, threaten or expose someone (doxxing).

Google weighs whether the information serves a public interest. A phone number on your personal blog that you published yourself, or a business landline on a company website, is far less likely to be removed than a private mobile number posted by a stranger in a forum thread.

Using "Results about you" step by step

The fastest route is the "Results about you" hub in your Google Account (in Italian, "Risultati che ti riguardano"), reachable from the Google app or from the menu beside a search result.

  1. Search for your name, address or phone number on Google and find the result that shows the data.
  2. Tap the three dots next to the result, open "About this result" and choose "Remove result".
  3. Select the reason, for example "It shows my personal contact info", and specify which item appears: address, phone or email.
  4. Confirm whether the data is visible on the page itself or only in Google's preview, then submit.
  5. Track the status in the same hub; Google sends an email when a decision is made.

Where the monitoring feature is available, you can also save your contact details so that Google alerts you when new results containing them appear. Coverage of this alert function has been expanding country by country, so Italian users should check their own account; the removal request itself works regardless. If Google rejects the request, it usually explains why, and a new submission with a clearer screenshot or a more precise URL is allowed.

Going to the source: the website owner

A successful Google request hides the page from search results only; the content stays on the site and remains reachable through other search engines, social shares and direct links. To make removal permanent, ask the publisher to delete your data.

A GDPR erasure request that gets answered

Article 17 GDPR gives you the right to obtain erasure of personal data that is no longer necessary or that is processed without a valid legal basis. A good request names the exact URL, identifies the data to delete, cites art. 17 and, where relevant, art. 21 (right to object), and asks for confirmation. Under art. 12 the controller must reply within one month, extendable by two further months for complex cases. Send it to the privacy contact or data protection officer listed in the site's privacy policy, by email or certified email (PEC) for Italian organisations, and keep proof of sending.

Telephone directories and Italian listings

If you want to remove a phone number from Google for good, start by checking where it originates: numbers that appear in online white pages often come from the public telephone directory. Under art. 129 of the Codice Privacy, inclusion in public directories depends on the subscriber's choice, so you can ask your phone operator to remove or limit your listing, and the change then flows to the directory sites that reuse that database.

When the publisher does not respond

Silence or a refusal without justification can be challenged before the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali through a complaint (reclamo). Websites hosted outside the EU that ignore requests are harder to reach legally, which is when the Google route becomes the main tool rather than a complement.

Clearing what Google still shows after the page changes

Once a site deletes your phone number or address, Google may keep displaying the old snippet until it recrawls the page. The public "Refresh outdated content" tool, part of Google's Search Console Removals family but usable without owning the website, asks Google to update or drop the stale result.

Paste the exact URL and, if the page still exists, the word that has disappeared from it, such as your street name. Google checks the live page; if the term is gone, the snippet is updated, and if the page returns a 404 or 410, the result is removed. This step matters because Italian address and phone data are often shown in cached previews long after the source has been corrected.

Addresses outside the search results page

To remove an address from Google Search completely, check the other Google surfaces where a home location can appear. Each has its own procedure:

Street View. Open the image of your house in Google Maps, use "Report a problem" and request blurring of the building. Blurring is permanent and cannot be reversed, so it suits people with a genuine safety concern.

Business Profile. Many Italian freelancers, therapists and craftsmen registered a Google Business Profile at their home. Switching to a service-area business hides the street address while keeping the listing active.

Knowledge panel and Maps contributions. If your home has been added to Maps as a place or appears in a panel about you, suggest an edit or use the feedback link to flag private information.

What usually stays online

Not every appearance of your contact details can be removed. Google generally keeps results where the information is part of a public or professional role and where you control the publication.

Removal works best for private data posted by others; it works poorly for data you are legally required, or chose, to make public.

Typical examples in Italy are the registered office of a company in the Registro delle Imprese, the PEC address of a professional enrolled in an official register (albo), and contact details in court rulings or official gazettes. For these, the realistic options are reducing duplication on secondary sites and building other results that outrank them, a distinction explained in our article on the difference between removal, deindexing and suppression. Requests involving names in news coverage follow a different test, covered in what the right to be forgotten can really remove.

The effort to remove personal information from Google is most effective when done in one pass: map every result that shows your data, file Google requests and GDPR letters in parallel, then verify after a few weeks.
